evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: We like to move fast and do work that matters. You'll be trusted to make important calls and to balance speed with rigour.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: The JD explicitly names both speed ('move fast') and rigour as equally weighted values to balance, an unambiguous mixed signal.
evidence.domain_risk: Dig into behavioural and financial data to find user segments, improve conversion, and understand the consumer life cycle in the app
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Errors affect product experimentation and internal decision-making at a wellness app without financial-reporting or regulatory-audit language, placing this at moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: An existing analytics engineering team with a modern stack (BigQuery, Looker, dbt) is described as growing, with the role explicitly tasked with helping 'grow the analytics engineering team' and moving toward more self-serve/agentic analytics, indicating an actively scaling but not yet fully mature function.
evidence.jd_authorship: Own how data comes in, how it's modelled, and the metrics people trust, using good software engineering practices to ship clean, documented, well-tested datasets
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name precise technical scope (BigQuery, Looker, dbt, semantic layers, agentic analytics, event-based datasets with varied schemas, causal inference) that shows exactly what the role does day to day, written by someone close to the work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: You'll measure and interpret the experiments that decide what we ship... A product mindset matters here.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role centers on A/B test analysis, product experimentation, and improving conversion/user segments within the app, a product orientation.
evidence.autonomy_level: As one of the most senior people in analytics, you'll set the technical bar, mentor other analytics engineers, and help us move toward more self-serve and agentic analytics
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role sets technical direction, mentors others, and drives the strategic shift toward self-serve/agentic analytics, all strategic direction-setting language.
evidence.ai_role: Experience with Python, LLM or agentic analytics workflows, and semantic layers
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate is expected to use LLM/agentic workflows as part of their own analytics tooling and to build agents that let others self-serve, primarily an ai_user signal for the candidate's own work, though it also touches ai_enabler-adjacent territory (building agents for others) — user dominates as the more concrete, testable requirement.
evidence.testing_framing: using good software engineering practices to ship clean, documented, well-tested datasets
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and documentation are framed as an owned responsibility with explicit ownership language ('own how data comes in... ship clean, documented, well-tested datasets'), not just a tool in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The JD is framed entirely in growth, ownership, and mission-driven terms ('reversing the modern day health pandemic') with no risk, compliance, or reliability register present.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Build the tooling, semantic layers and agents that let the rest of the company answer their own questions, so analytics scales beyond the team
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The JD mixes new-build language (build tooling, semantic layers, agents) with existing-metric-ownership language (own how data comes in, metrics people trust) roughly evenly, making this mixed.
evidence.work_arrangement: The role is fully remote, but you must be based in Australia
